messages:
julia: Customer (acct: acme-plat) reporting intermittent 502/504 on hosted API since 08:39 UTC. They say calls spike with short sequences, ~50 concurrent reqs, and errors surface within tail 1-2s. They attached a couple request IDs.

omar: can you paste the req ids? also which model/route?

julia: reqs: rQ0f3, rQ0f4. Route: /v1/chat.generate model=redwood-1-medium, no functions, standard system+user prompt. Token counts small.

lucas: I'm seeing elevated gateway 502s in the hosted-api LB at 08:38-08:44 and lots of backend timeouts to runtime instances. Latency SLO breaches for 99th.

renee: infra alert fired: redis-prefix-cluster -> clients_rejected high, evictions up, and tcp resets. infra-bot shows memcache/redis both in stack for prefix caching, but master redis node had a flapping event.

infra-bot: Alert: redis-prefix-01: maxclients=100% at 2026-03-15T08:37:54Z. Node down: redis-prefix-02 at 08:36:52Z.

ethan: runtime's caching layer (prefixKV) assumes cache calls are fast. When the KV layer blocks, the worker goroutine waits and request processing queue backs up -> LB sees backend as slow -> 502. We need an immediate bypass to reduce customer impact.

julia: customer is losing production traffic. they are asking for ETA and mitigation.

omar: short term: flip prefix cache to passive mode (reads bypass, writes stop) for hosted pool. I can push a flag via config service. Doing canary on a subset of instances.

deploy-bot: config change initiated by omar: feature.flag.prefix_cache=passive -> canary 10% at 08:42 UTC.

omar: canary logs show for canary traffic redis errors vanish and 502s drop on those instances. promoting to 100% now.

deploy-bot: promotion to 100% complete at 08:45 UTC.

lucas: backend timeouts reduced, customer reports drop in errors to <5%. Good temporary win.

renee: infra team restarted redis-prefix-02, resharded some hot keys and bound memory limits. Found many keys with no TTL on prefix-cache leading to unbounded growth.

infra-bot: redis logs excerpt:

```
Mar 15 08:35:12 redis-prefix-02 redis-server[1234]: WARNING: maxclients reached (maxclients=1024)
Mar 15 08:36:10 redis-prefix-02 redis-server[1234]: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
Mar 15 08:37:01 redis-prefix-02 redis-server[1234]: Connection reset by peer
```

ethan: looks like a classic hot-prefix + no TTL + client-side connection leak. Also saw memcached backends returning 504 in traces when redis struggled -> polycache layer doesn't degrade cleanly.

omar: root cause hypothesis: sudden customer traffic pattern created many new prefix keys (hot prefixes). Redis node hit mem pressure and maxclients, connections queued, some client library versions block pipelines on slow responses. Runtime didn't convert cache client failures into fast misses, so upstream requests waited and triggered gateway timeouts/502s.

julia: customer update sent: short summary + mitigation (we bypassed prefix cache), and we promised RCA. They asked about retries and cost impact.

ethan: longer-term fixes I propose: 1) runtime defensive changes to treat cache errors as miss quickly (nonblocking) 2) add circuit-breaker + token-bucket per instance for cache calls 3) ensure prefix keys have TTL and enforce max key cardinality per tenant 4) upgrade redis client lib to one with non-blocking pools 5) add sentinel/proxy improvements & increase maxclients and tune eviction policy 6) add synthetic load test for hot-prefix patterns.

renee: infra actions: apply TTL default 1h for prefix cache keys; increase maxclients by 20%; add alert for key growth > threshold; schedule maintenance to move very hot prefixes to dedicated cache nodes.

omar: quick runtime patch I will land (non-blocking fallback):

```
// prefix_fallback.go
func GetWithTimeout(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]byte, bool) {
  ctx2, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 50*time.Millisecond)
  defer cancel()
  val, err := client.GetWithContext(ctx2, key)
  if err != nil {
    metrics.Count("prefix_cache.fallback", 1)
    return nil, false // treat as miss, continue request
  }
  return val, true
}
```

omar: PR to be merged today, deploy in next runtime rollout.

ethan: also we'll add telemetry: prefix_cache.latency_p99, connection_errors, evictions_count to make SLA impact visible.

julia: billing: customer saw retries but token counts look normal; will confirm with billing if any charges from retries above expected.

support-bot: Incident logged INC-20260315-022. Postmortem requested.

julia: timeline for customer: initial report 08:39 UTC, bypass pushed 08:45 UTC, infra restart 08:48 UTC, errors baseline resume 08:52 UTC. I'll schedule a follow-up call with acme-plat tomorrow.

renee: I'll write infra section of RCA, include graphs of redis maxclients, memory, and key counts.

omar: I'll own runtime PRs and a release note for the fallback behavior.

julia: thanks all. keeping thread open until RCA lands. :thumbsup:
